01 / Foundations & ownership

Foundations & ownership

The world foundations, mission intent and operating roles. Units are controllable entities; agents decide; World Masters govern; systems implement the work.

01Worlddurable knowledge across local views

The world owns committed entities, evidence, progressive local maps, missions and executions across worker and agent resets. One logical world does not imply one coordinate frame. Original local observations retain their provenance when Units reconcile spatial views. Missing alignment does not prevent useful local knowledge.

one durable world · independent local frames · evidence-backed reconciliation
02Entityidentity independent of labels and trackers

An entity identifies a robot, object or other thing across observations. A new classification does not rename it. Association uses evidence to connect producer-scoped tracks to stable identities; matching labels alone are not enough.

backpack-A remains the same entity as its measurements change
03Unitan entity with controllable capabilities

A Go2, robot vacuum, simulated robot or motorized door can be a Unit. A chair is normally just an entity. Unit is a capability-based role, not a second identity or a competing entity hierarchy. Installed action bindings make control possible; an agent assignment makes requesting those actions permitted. An offline Unit remains a Unit, but unavailable. The concrete protocol below implements approach@1 as its first example, not every device capability.

Unit ⊂ Entity · capability ≠ permission ≠ availability
04Agenta logical decision-maker, independent of hardware

An agent coordinates assigned missions and controlled Units using automatically prepared world context. Agents can collaborate through shared mission facts and addressed messages. Eve owns reasoning history; Nemeia owns durable world state. Perception, mapping and control systems work independently at their own rates.

mission log + Unit authority + automatic world context
05World Masterthe privileged client that governs missions and assignments

A human or authorized automation sets missions, assigns participating agents, grants Unit control and read scope, and supervises outcomes. Its client can inspect the whole recorded world, pause agents, reassign resources and intervene through audited operations. This is a permissioned role, not a mandatory singleton service or a special kind of LLM. It sees known evidence, not physical omniscience; it cannot falsify observations or bypass local safety.

World Masters assign missions · agents coordinate Units · systems execute
06Componenttyped state with evidence and time

Components describe facets such as pose, geometry, semantics and robot control. Each observed facet retains its acquisition time, version and provenance. Missing values stay unknown; a label update cannot make stale geometry fresh.

entity + independently timed facets
07Relationshipa directed fact between entities

Relationships connect existing entities using a defined predicate. Observed relationships retain evidence; configured facts remain distinguishable. Removal must preserve reference integrity, rather than leaving dangling endpoints.

subject + predicate + object
08Affordancewhat an unit could do in the current situation

An affordance evaluates an action's requirements against current evidence at a known time. It is a useful read-only hint, not permission to execute. The action boundary repeats freshness, identity and policy checks when accepting a request.

unit + target + requirements → availability and reasons
09Actionintent with bounded execution and a measured outcome

An action names an operation with typed inputs, requirements and an installed implementation. Each request has one stable execution identity. Simulation and physical bindings share intent; hardware additionally enforces local limits, stop and durable receipts. A sent command is not a successful outcome.

intent → admission → execution → evidence
10Systemsoftware for a specific job, at its own cadence

Perception, association, classification, pathfinding and control adapters can use specialized models or deterministic logic. They do not each need an agent, a mission or a reasoning loop. Agents choose intent at a higher level; systems turn accepted intent into plans, bounded execution and measured feedback. Inference and physical IO remain outside transactions. An interface does not require a separate microservice.

observation clock ≠ decision clock ≠ physical control clock
11Eventa recorded occurrence, not just the latest value

Events preserve important transitions and outcomes that current state alone may hide. Clients retain must-handle events until acknowledged. World audit, client attention and diagnostic traces have different retention needs; an update callback is not durable history. Full scene replay needs a separately specified recorder.

current state ≠ important transitions ≠ diagnostic traces
12Missiondescription, objectives and validated progress

A World Master describes the work, defines objectives and assigns an agent. One agent coordinates multiple assignments through its mission log. Mission definitions and objective progress belong to the shared world, not a model conversation or a second board database. Validated evidence advances objectives; linked physical work must close safely before the mission ends.

description + objectives → assignment → mission log → objective progress
02 / Objects & world view

Objects & world view

WorldView projects durable entities, evidence, local maps, missions and executions. Each spatial estimate retains its coordinate frame and acquisition time.

01Geometry & sensor referencesnative SDK algebraic types

The four geometry names are Nemeia tags, not an external standard. The SDK encodes union values as {tag,value}. Geometry follows ROS coordinate and unit conventions; reducers still validate finite values, positive sizes and quaternion norms.

export const Vec3 = t.object("Vec3", {
  x: t.f64(), // finite x, meters when used for positions or dimensions
  y: t.f64(), // finite y
  z: t.f64(), // finite z
});
export const Quaternion = t.object("Quaternion", {
  x: t.f64(), y: t.f64(), z: t.f64(), w: t.f64(), // unit quaternion, ROS [x,y,z,w] order
});
export const Pose3 = t.object("Pose3", {
  positionM: Vec3, // translation in the containing coordinate frame
  orientation: Quaternion, // unit rotation; reject invalid norms
});
export const FrameRef = t.object("FrameRef", {
  streamId: t.string(), // camera, LiDAR or another sensor stream
  sessionId: t.string(), // changes when the stream restarts
  sequence: t.u64(), // sample number within the stream session
  capturedAt: t.timestamp(), // acquisition time mapped to the world clock
});
export const ResourceRef = t.object("ResourceRef", {
  id: t.string(), // immutable stored bytes; not a URL or live stream
  schema: t.string(), // exact encoding/version, e.g. sensor_msgs/PointCloud2
  sha256: t.string(), // digest of retained bytes; storage confirms persistence first
});
export const Geometry = t.enum("Geometry", {
  boundingBox3D: t.object("BoundingBox3D", {
    frameId: t.string(), pose: Pose3, sizeM: Vec3, // center pose and full positive dimensions
  }),
  boundingBox2D: t.object("BoundingBox2D", {
    frame: FrameRef, // exact image, not the world map
    centerX: t.f64(), centerY: t.f64(), // pixels
    width: t.f64(), height: t.f64(), angleRad: t.f64(), // full extents and rotation
  }),
  pointCloud: t.object("PointCloud", {
    frameId: t.string(), resource: ResourceRef, // cloud bytes stay outside the live database
  }),
  mesh: t.object("Mesh", {
    frameId: t.string(), pose: Pose3, resource: ResourceRef, // vertices and topology in retained bytes
  }),
}); // SDK unions use { tag, value }; these four names remain Nemeia's geometry tags
export type Geometry = Infer<typeof Geometry>;
export type Pose3 = Infer<typeof Pose3>;
export type FrameRef = Infer<typeof FrameRef>;
export type ResourceRef = Infer<typeof ResourceRef>;
02Observations & provenanceindependently timed, partial facets

Evidence retains acquisition times, source frames, exact transforms and fusion predecessors. Identity comes from authenticated association. Absent facets do not erase current components; delayed evidence must not replace newer samples.

export const PackagePin = t.object("PackagePin", {
  name: t.string(), version: t.string(), sha256: t.string(), // immutable producing/executing code
});
export const Semantic = t.object("Semantic", {
  hypotheses: t.array(t.object("Hypothesis", {
    label: t.string(), score: t.f64(), // model score in [0,1], not physical capability
  })),
});
export const PoseSample = t.object("PoseSample", {
  observedAt: t.timestamp(), frameId: t.string(), value: Pose3, // acquisition time, not database arrival
});
export const GeometrySample = t.object("GeometrySample", {
  observedAt: t.timestamp(), value: Geometry, // independent geometry timestamp
});
export const SemanticSample = t.object("SemanticSample", {
  observedAt: t.timestamp(), value: Semantic, // a new label does not refresh geometry
});
export const TransformSample = t.object("TransformSample", {
  parentFrameId: t.string(), childFrameId: t.string(), // transform maps child coordinates into parent
  observedAt: t.timestamp(), pose: Pose3, // exact acquisition-time transform, not the latest one
});
export const ObservationInput = t.object("ObservationInput", {
  id: t.string(), // UUID; identical retries are no-ops, changed payloads are conflicts
  localMapId: t.string(), // originating local-map context, validated against producer authority; retain even for unlocated evidence
  producerSession: t.string(), // must match the authenticated member's current producer session
  trackId: t.option(t.string()), // scoped to identity + producer session; never a label
  entityId: t.option(t.string()), // trusted association hint; reducer checks allowed entity/facet ownership
  inputs: t.array(FrameRef), // evidence references do not promise recorded bytes
  retained: t.array(ResourceRef), // only resources already durably stored
  transforms: t.array(TransformSample), // coordinate conversions used by this observation
  supersedes: t.array(t.string()), // validated predecessor observation IDs for fusion provenance
  pose: t.option(PoseSample), // omitted facet leaves the current component unchanged
  geometry: t.option(GeometrySample), // at least one of pose, geometry, semantic must be present
  semantic: t.option(SemanticSample), // each supplied facet has its own freshness and ownership checks
});
export type ObservationInput = Infer<typeof ObservationInput>;
export type PackagePin = Infer<typeof PackagePin>;
export type TransformSample = Infer<typeof TransformSample>;
03Action request & resultone attempt, one receipt

The approach@1 contract illustrates a typed action with explicit inputs and admission checks. It may serve a direct approach objective or a scoped investigation, but arrival alone cannot complete a search or inspection. Each installed action follows the same intent, execution and receipt boundary. A running row means claimed; it does not prove physical motion.

export const MissionLink = t.object("MissionLink", {
  missionId: t.string(), objectiveId: t.string(), // mission and ready objective this attempt serves; investigation actions do not themselves complete it
  expectedRevision: t.u64(), // admission and claim reject a closing, terminal or changed mission
});
export const ApproachRequest = t.object("ApproachRequest", {
  executionId: t.string(), // caller-generated UUID; both attempt identity and retry key
  unitId: t.string(), // controllable entity chosen by an agent; never a separate robot identity
  assignment: t.option(t.object("AssignmentPin", {
    agentId: t.string(), revision: t.u64(), // verify caller mapping, current Unit grant, allowed action and expiry at admission AND claim
  })), // required for agents; absent only on the explicit World Master intervention path
  targetId: t.string(), // existing entity with usable 3D geometry
  standoffM: t.f64(), // positive ground-plane distance to target center; not obstacle clearance
  expectedGeometryFrameId: t.string(), // identify the exact frame-qualified target facet; require a usable transform to the executor
  expectedGeometryVersion: t.u64(), // reject if the selected target changed since the client read it
  acceptBy: t.timestamp(), // short acceptance deadline; not a physical motion deadline
  mission: t.option(MissionLink), // required for agents; absent only for an audited standalone World Master intervention
});
export type ApproachRequest = Infer<typeof ApproachRequest>;
export const ExecutionState = t.enum("ExecutionState", [
  "accepted", "running", "cancelling", "succeeded", "cancelled", "failed",
]); // terminal states are immutable; running means claimed, not proof of motion
export const Completion = t.enum("Completion", {
  succeeded: t.object("ApproachResult", {
    distanceM: t.f64(), // measured distance, checked against unit/target observations
    unitObservationId: t.string(), targetObservationId: t.string(), // exact final measurements
    localReceiptId: t.string(), // durable controller receipt confirming safe closure
  }),
  cancelled: t.object("Cancelled", { localReceiptId: t.string() }), // safe state confirmed
  failed: t.object("Failed", {
    code: t.string(), detail: t.string(), // e.g. stale_evidence, watchdog, outcome_unknown
    localReceiptId: t.option(t.string()), // absent when the physical outcome cannot be established
  }),
});
export type Completion = Infer<typeof Completion>;
export const Role = t.enum("Role", ["viewer", "world_master", "agent", "perception", "controller", "admin"]); // admin provisions; World Master governs missions; neither overrides local safety
export const Mode = t.enum("Mode", ["simulation", "physical"]);
// For approached, require the specified target/standoff. For located or inspected, investigation may
// precede place resolution. Require measured local targets within separately authorized exploration limits.
// This action can support an investigation, but only the objective criterion determines progress.
04Pose navigation & action outcomesnavigate@1 and approach@1 share one execution boundary

Pose navigation reaches a map-derived viewpoint without inventing an opening or destination entity. Nemeia adds authority, evidence and retry semantics around the installed navigation adapter. Local planning and control enforce Unit-specific traversability; the page does not assume a navigation stack is already available on Go2.

type NavigateRequest = Pick<ApproachRequest,
  "executionId" | "unitId" | "assignment" | "acceptBy" | "mission"
> & {
  mapId: string; basisMapRevision: bigint; // checkpoint used to choose the viewpoint; not a frozen safety map
  frameId: string; targetPose: Pose3; // measured-map-derived pose, never coordinates invented from a room name
};
type ActionIntent =
  | { tag: "approach"; value: ApproachRequest } // approach@1: maintain a standoff from an observed entity
  | { tag: "navigate"; value: NavigateRequest }; // navigate@1: reach a specific local pose
interface NavigationResult {
  unitObservationId: string; localReceiptId: string; // final measured pose and durable safe-closure receipt
} // Validate position and heading against installed tolerances; arrival does not prove an inspection result.
type ActionCompletion = Exclude<Completion, { tag: "succeeded" }> | {
  tag: "succeeded";
  value:
    | { tag: "approach"; value: Extract<Completion, { tag: "succeeded" }>["value"] }
    | { tag: "navigate"; value: NavigationResult }; // outcome must match the accepted action
};
// Nemeia's admission envelope wraps a pose-navigation pattern such as Nav2 NavigateToPose.
// The installed adapter supplies the behavior tree, footprint, traversability and motion policy.
// Admission/claim check current localization, grants and permitted exploration bounds.
// Local planning checks live obstacles continuously; a retained map is never a safety clearance.
// A new map revision triggers revalidation, not automatic cancellation on every mapping update.
// Reject a reset frame or an invalidated viewpoint. Unknown space is not implicitly drivable.
05Spatial layers, regions & namesmetric structure and semantic meaning stay separate

Native occupancy and surface products accumulate independently of object detection. Regions delimit space in a retained checkpoint. Models propose semantic hypotheses; a World Master assigns a name with provenance. Region identity, mapped extent and human name can evolve independently.

interface MapLayer {
  kind: "occupancy" | "surface"; // free/occupied/unknown cells or measured 3D surfaces; different products
  resource: ResourceRef; // exact native encoding/version: e.g. nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid or sensor_msgs/PointCloud2
  observedAt: Timestamp; // newest included acquisition; per-cell/point age and coverage remain in retained provenance
} // Resource payload carries resolution, origin and encoding. A cloud is not an occupancy grid.
interface MapCheckpoint {
  mapId: string; frameId: string; // independent local map and immutable coordinate epoch
  revision: bigint; parentRevision?: bigint; // retained checkpoint lineage
}
interface LocalMapRecord {
  id: string; unitId: string; rootFrameId: string; // durable map identity, originating Unit and immutable frame
  revision: bigint; headRevisionId?: string; createdAt: Timestamp; // committed head, not current localization
}
interface SpatialFrameRecord {
  id: string; unitId?: string; // new identity for each coordinate reset
  kind: "local_map" | "odom" | "body" | "sensor" | "site"; createdAt: Timestamp; // registered frame role
}
interface MapRevisionRecord {
  id: string; mapId: string; revision: bigint; parentRevision?: bigint; // immutable checkpoint lineage
  manifest: ResourceRef; recordedAt: Timestamp; // retained payload and commit time, not sensor freshness
}
interface RegionExtent {
  mapRevision: bigint; // exact retained checkpoint used to delimit this region
  occupancyResourceId: string; // occupancy layer in that checkpoint; establishes grid origin/resolution/frame
  mask: ResourceRef; // sensor_msgs/Image mono8: same grid dimensions and cell ordering; 1 = included, 0 = outside
  coverage: "partial" | "bounded"; // partial is explored extent only; bounded means its boundary is established
} // Image row y matches occupancy row y, with no display-axis flip; validate step/encoding and resource frame.
// This alignment/encoding is Nemeia's convention over ROS messages, not a ROS room standard.
// Bounding a region does not prove every cell is observed, unobstructed or traversable by a Unit.
interface RegionName {
  text: string; assignedBy: Identity; assignedAt: Timestamp; // World Master annotation, not a detector score
}
interface RegionRecord {
  entityId: string; mapId: string; // region reuses Entity identity; neither a label nor a coordinate frame
  revision: bigint; // compare-and-set for extent or name edits; never use map revision as this fence
  extent: RegionExtent; // progressively refined spatial membership, independent of the name
  observationIds: readonly string[]; // retained spatial evidence behind the extent
  name?: RegionName; // absent while unnamed; model proposals stay in semantic.hypotheses
}
interface RegionView {
  region: Readonly<RegionRecord>; // small current component; masks remain in resource storage
  hypotheses: readonly { label: string; score: number }[]; // derived semantic component, not assigned names
  objectIds: readonly string[]; // evidenced located_in relations; not a permanent object-ownership list
  connectedRegionIds: readonly string[]; // evidenced topology, not a claim that a path is safe
} // Region IDs survive renaming and boundary refinement. Split/merge requires explicit identity review.
// Keep old extents and their evidence reachable from mission proofs; renaming never rewrites old findings.
06World view & affordancesdurable local knowledge, read-only projection

WorldView exposes accumulated entities, independent local views and mission progress. Persist underlying records and map resources, not a second WorldView snapshot. Adapters preserve timestamp, identity and revision semantics when serializing the projection.

// Authorized read projection over durable world records.
interface WorldView {
  worldId: string; // shared durable domain, not a promise of one coordinate system
  entities: ReadonlyMap<string, EntityView>; // authorized identities and current evidence-backed facets
  localMaps: readonly LocalMapView[]; // independent progressive maps; alignment is not assumed
  units: ReadonlyMap<string, UnitView>; // controllable entities, with the same entity IDs
  missions: ReadonlyMap<string, MissionView>; // intent and verified progress survive an Eve session reset
  agents: ReadonlyMap<string, AgentView>; // logical decision-makers and their authorized assignments
  relationships: readonly Row<"relation">[]; // configured or evidenced links; not automatic spatial alignment
  executions: readonly Row<"execution">[]; // durable intent and receipts, when an action is used
  actions: readonly Row<"actionBinding">[]; // installed capabilities; unavailable actions carry explicit reasons
  synchronized: boolean; // fresh authorized subscription state, not proof of live localization
} // Read projection over durable world records, never another writable snapshot or Eve memory store.
interface EntityView {
  entity: Readonly<Row<"entity">>; // stable identity; provisional association does not prove global identity
  poses: readonly Row<"pose">[]; // frame-qualified estimates; never force one global pose
  geometries: readonly Row<"geometry">[]; // preserve image-space evidence and local metric estimates separately
  semantic?: Readonly<Row<"semantic">>; // model hypotheses do not fabricate positions or assign human names
  region?: Readonly<RegionRecord>; // a spatial region is an Entity with an extent, not a special identity system
  control?: Readonly<Row<"unitControl">>; // measured local control projection for a Unit
}
interface Affordance {
  unitId: string; targetId?: string; // action-specific target; observation alone need not be spatially located
  evaluatedAt: Timestamp; // evidence continues to age without a new database write
  available: boolean; reasons: readonly string[]; // e.g. target_unlocated or relocalization_required
} // Check only the spatial requirements of this action; admission repeats them against current evidence.
07LocalMapView & checkpoint manifestprogressive, retained and recoverable

A local map exposes spatial layers, regions, tracked entities and unlocated evidence. A checkpoint pins native products and archived component versions; current rows may be newer. Restore both after restart without treating a retained map as a current localized Unit.

interface LocalMapView {
  map: Readonly<LocalMapRecord>; // durable identity, root frame and committed checkpoint head
  frames: readonly SpatialFrameRecord[]; // immutable frame identities, including distinct reset epochs
  checkpoint?: Readonly<MapRevisionRecord>; // absent before the first map checkpoint; observations still persist
  layers: readonly MapLayer[]; // checkpoint products: accumulated surfaces and/or occupancy, not just object detections
  regions: readonly RegionView[]; // partial or bounded spaces; names and hypotheses can be absent
  entityIds: readonly string[]; // derived local membership, not an agent subscription or permission list
  unlocatedObservationIds: readonly string[]; // known evidence that cannot yet be positioned in this map
  localization: "localized" | "relocalization_required" | "unavailable"; // derived from current qualified evidence
} // Restoring map bytes does not restore knowledge of the Unit's current position.
interface LocalMapManifest extends MapCheckpoint {
  evidenceIndex: ResourceRef; // retained index of exact input observations/resources and source-session boundaries
  layers: readonly MapLayer[]; // complete retained products; each native payload includes frame and spatial metadata
  regionVersions: readonly { entityId: string; revision: bigint }[]; // exact archived region components at this checkpoint
  estimatorState?: ResourceRef; // optional versioned native export; not a guarantee of localization after restart
  producer: PackagePin; // exact mapper implementation; calibration/transform provenance stays with its inputs
} // Layers may be empty before metric mapping. Paged native products retain their full resource closure.
// Current region/entity components can advance independently of this checkpoint; expose their own basis revisions.
// Publish all referenced bytes first, then atomically commit map_revision + local_map head + audit.
// Keep evidence and checkpoint ancestry reachable under retention policy; never publish a dangling head.
08MissionViewdescription, objectives and derived objective progress

Join the authorized mission, assignment and mission_objective_progress records. Include pending objectives even when they have no progress row. Derive readiness using the same graph semantics as admission; these fields are hints, not permission.

interface MissionView {
  mission: Readonly<Mission>; // accepted specification and authoritative lifecycle
  objectiveProgress: readonly ObjectiveProgress[]; // one derived entry for every objective, including pending ones
  readyObjectiveIds: readonly string[]; // pending objectives whose dependencies are complete, while active and before deadline
  participants: readonly Row<"missionAgent">[]; // World Master assignments; separate from Unit authority
} // Join mission + mission_objective_progress + mission_agent; do not persist this view.
// Ready means eligible for work, not that a Unit is available or an action is safe.
09UnitView & AgentViewcontrollable entities and independent decision-makers

Units reuse entity identity. Agents have separate durable identities, mission participation and resource assignments. One command-owning agent holds the Unit grant; observers and advisers do not need control ownership.

interface UnitView extends EntityView {
  bindings: readonly Row<"actionBinding">[]; // installed controllable capabilities; no second Unit identity
  assignment?: Readonly<Row<"unitAssignment">>; // command authority, not an execution reservation
  localMapId?: string; // current local mapping context; absent or unlocalized does not erase observations
}
interface AgentView {
  agent: Readonly<Row<"agent">>; // stable identity and world-managed access/pause
  missionLog: MissionLog; // all assigned missions and their progress; not one mission per agent
  assignments: readonly Row<"unitAssignment">[]; // authoritative Unit grants
  localMapIds: readonly string[]; // derived awareness of assigned Units; the agent does not choose subscriptions
} // Eve owns runtime history. Nemeia owns recoverable world memory and derives bounded step context.
02a / World memory & local maps

World memory & local maps

The world retains accumulated knowledge across observations and restarts. Units can maintain independent spatial views and reconcile them through qualified frame relationships.

01Durable world stateshared knowledge independent of agent memory

Observations accumulate into durable entities, evidence and progressive local maps. Mission progress, assignments and execution receipts share this world state. Agents read relevant projections; they do not own separate copies of the world. Persistence is a platform responsibility and survives worker restarts or Eve session resets.

observe → commit → refine → recover → continue
02Progressive local mapspatial structure grows before rooms have names

A mapping system combines ranging with IMU/odometry and, where supported, visual measurements. It estimates Unit motion and accumulates surfaces or an occupancy representation with free, occupied and unknown space. Store these native products as retained resources, not one Entity per point or cell. Image detections add object knowledge without replacing the spatial map. Unknown depth stays unknown. A partial point cloud does not prove free space, full object dimensions or search coverage.

range + motion estimates → accumulated spatial map · images → semantic evidence
03Regions, labels and objectsmap geometry → stable regions → revisable meaning

Spatial processing delimits regions and observed connections from accumulated geometry. A region is an Entity with a versioned extent; it can remain partial and unnamed. Semantic workers propose room hypotheses. A World Master can assign a name such as Kitchen before the map is complete. Names are not unique IDs and do not change coordinate frames. Objects have independent tracks and evidence-backed located_in relations. Refining a boundary or renaming a region preserves identity and historical evidence; splitting or merging regions requires explicit identity review.

space-2 + measured extent + Kitchen · backpack-A located_in space-1
04Calibrated perception fusionparallel geometry and vision, then qualified association

Match camera detections or masks to compatible range measurements using acquisition times, camera intrinsics, distortion, sensor extrinsics and pose history. Compensate motion where needed and reject occluded or inconsistent matches. Preserve image-only observations when association is unsupported. A planar LiDAR cannot measure full object height; a partial surface cannot silently become a complete measured box. Associate repeated views into the same object only with evidence of continuity. Geometry, semantics and visibility keep independent times.

mapping + image evidence → calibrated association → persistent object tracks
05Durability and recoveryworld persistence is independent of Eve history

Persist current world rows, retained supporting observations and versioned map checkpoints. Store large geometry and optional native estimator exports as immutable resources. Validate retained bytes before advancing a checkpoint head atomically; preserve its exact evidence coverage. After a crash, restore the last committed head and reconcile later retained observations by their IDs, without pretending an audit log is a full scene recorder. A mapper that cannot resume its native state starts a new frame epoch until it can relocalize. An Eve reset changes conversation history, not map, mission, entity or execution identity.

restored map ≠ localized Unit · durable world ≠ conversation transcript
06Automatic Unit awarenessdirect observations first; radius when usable

Nemeia derives agent context from assigned Units. It always includes their permitted observations, mission dependencies and pending outcomes. A world-managed radius adds nearby shared state only when metric positions can be compared reliably. Discovery and unlocated evidence remain outside radius filtering. No agent-managed subscriptions or preselected entity list. As context grows, keep bounded relevant projections and authorized detail reads; absence from a prompt never deletes durable world knowledge.

Unit observations + usable local neighborhood + mission dependencies → context
07Local frames and reconciliationone logical world; independent spatial views

Every metric estimate names its frame and acquisition time. Register fresh frame identities after coordinate resets; never reinterpret old coordinates. Local sensor transforms remain necessary when fusing measurements. Cross-Unit alignment is optional: a qualified localization system publishes evidence-backed relationships between frames when available. Keep original local evidence and identity provenance; aligning maps does not prove two tracks are the same object. Agents can share non-spatial mission findings without aligned coordinates.

local frame A · local frame B · evidence-backed relationship
08Spatial requirements belong to actionssemantic destinations resolve to measured local goals

A room description resolves to an evidenced region, then its current extent and a useful viewing or navigation pose. An unresolved description triggers observation or authorized exploration, not fabricated coordinates. navigate@1 targets a pose; approach@1 targets an observed entity at a standoff. Both require current localization and qualified local planning. The controller derives a Unit-specific cost/traversability view and checks live obstacles independently of mapping and LLM rates. Another Unit needs qualified alignment or independent reacquisition.

kitchen → region identity → current extent → local pose → planner + control
02b / Missions & mission log

Missions & mission log

Description explains the work. Objectives define success. The agent coordinates its assignments through a mission log. The world validates objective progress.

01Descriptionthe outcome and context supplied by the World Master

MissionSpec.description explains the work, like a quest briefing. It provides context, not a completion predicate. Objectives define what counts as success. Keep the accepted specification inline in the mission row, with an optional template pin for provenance. Validate known references, but allow place descriptions such as the kitchen to remain unresolved at creation. Discovering the place is part of the mission. Evidence must establish which place was found and what was inspected before completion; names alone supply no geometry or control permission. A changed description or objective creates a new mission; changing strategy does not.

description explains why · objectives define what must be demonstrated
02Objectives & dependenciesoutcome graph, not a fixed action script

Each objective has a stable ID, a typed criterion and an all-of dependency list. Independent objectives can progress in parallel. Optional objectives do not block completion and cannot be prerequisites of required ones. Reject duplicate IDs, missing references, cycles, empty required sets and graphs above 32 nodes. These are milestones: acquiring geometry once does not mean it stays fresh forever. Continuous conditions remain action admission and local-control checks.

geometry + semantics → approach → fresh geometry
03Objective progressvalidated evidence, not an agent's completion claim

The world records one immutable completion proof per objective in mission_objective_progress. The view includes pending objectives too, derived from the specification. An observed criterion checks the target, requested facet, acquisition time and evidence access; it proves a measurement exists, not that a classification is certainly true. Motion criteria require a matching measured execution outcome. Located and inspected criteria accept typed findings under explicit World Master review: identity, local evidence and inspection scope are checked separately. Obstructed can complete inspection; unknown cannot. Reviewed clear findings require coverage of the whole named region. Repeated delivery cannot inflate progress. The same evidence can advance several objectives only after each validates independently.

retained evidence + criterion-specific acceptance → objective progress
04Lifecycle & safe closureactive → closing → terminal

Creation activates an authorized specification. Described places may remain unresolved while the agent investigates; movement still requires independent authority and qualified local evidence. All required credits request success; cancellation requests cancellation; a deadline requests failure. Closing blocks new admission and claim, requests cancellation of unfinished linked attempts and waits for confirmed safe closure. Terminal failure with an unknown physical outcome is not safe closure. Cancellation may replace pending success until terminal commit; once terminal, the mission is immutable. A deadline reached during closing also prevents success. A failed action does not automatically fail the mission: a fresh attempt is possible while active, but first reconcile the old attempt.

goal achieved ≠ all physical work safely closed
05Mission logall assignments for one agent; the mission board

A World Master creates missions, then assigns the agent responsible for them. One agent can hold multiple assignments. Its mission log joins those assignments with descriptions, objectives, progress and outcomes; it is not another writable mission store or an event history. The agent coordinates work across the log. Selecting a focus does not pause other missions, stop their deadlines or prevent independent evidence from advancing them. Assignment and Unit grants remain separate.

World Master assigns → agent's mission log → selected work → shared progress
06Cross-mission coordinationone agent loop, several active missions

Nemeia prepares a compact summary of every assignment plus relevant changes, evidence, available Units and outstanding executions. The agent chooses its next work and reads details as needed. A blocked mission does not block the whole log. If no useful work is possible, wait for relevant changes or deadlines instead of repeatedly invoking the model. A Unit reservation applies across missions; switching attention is not physical cancellation. Eve owns the agent loop, not a separate loop per mission.

all assignments visible · bounded detail · one coordinated decision loop
07MMO referencespatterns borrowed and adapted
Definition vs progress
AzerothCore quest definitions and character quest status separate reusable content from a participant's progress. Nemeia adopts that distinction, with an inline immutable specification per mission.
Objective composition
EQEmu task activities define typed goals, counts, optional activities and ordered steps. Nemeia uses typed milestones and explicit dependencies to describe required outcomes.
Typed objective records
TrinityCore's QuestObjective separates objective identity, type, target and amount. Nemeia follows the typed-objective pattern but replaces gameplay credit with validated domain evidence.

These are primary references for open-source MMO server implementations, not claims about Blizzard's or Daybreak's internal databases. The Nemeia adaptation below is a design decision, not an MMO standard.

01PlaceTargetknown place or description to discover

A mission can name a place that has no entity or map location yet. Perception supplies candidates; evidence and review establish the referent. Ambiguity calls for more observation or clarification, not a fabricated room ID. Completion records the accepted place without rewriting the mission.

type PlaceTarget =
  | { tag: "entity"; value: { entityId: string } } // a known place identity; validate access and existence
  | { tag: "description"; value: { text: string } }; // e.g. "the kitchen"; no entity or location assumed
// A described place may be unresolved when the mission is created and assigned.
// Discovery associates retained observations with candidate place entities, not invented room IDs.
// A candidate label is a hypothesis. Several matches require more evidence or clarification.
// Accepted findings identify the discovered place and cite evidence tying it to this description.
// Preserve the original mission wording; discovering its referent does not rewrite MissionSpec.
// Place identity, geometric extent, and a safe route are separate questions.
// Mission wording never expands Unit authority or the controller's permitted exploration boundary.
02ObjectiveSpec & criterionexplicit conditions with typed validators

Keep explanatory text separate from measurable conditions. Observed and approached use retained measurements and execution receipts. Located searches for an initially unknown object; inspected reports a bounded region. Both reviewed criteria require World Master acceptance of a typed finding, not an LLM completion claim.

type ObjectiveCriterion =
  | { tag: "observed"; value: {
      entityId: string; // existing target identity, bound before mission creation
      facet: { tag: "geometry" | "semantic" }; // which retained measurement is required
      maxAgeMs: number; // positive u32; maximum acquisition age when progress is recorded
    } }
  | { tag: "approached"; value: {
      targetId: string; // motion objective; requires qualified local navigation
      standoffM: number; // finite positive target distance in meters
    } }
  | { tag: "located"; value: {
      description: string; // what to find; no target entity or destination must already exist
      searchArea: PlaceTarget; // where the object is sought; may begin as an unresolved place description
      maxAgeMs: number; // positive maximum acquisition age when the finding is accepted
      review: "world_master"; // explicit acceptance policy; a detector label cannot approve its own match
    } }
  | { tag: "inspected"; value: {
      region: PlaceTarget; // what to inspect; discovery may establish identity and extent during the mission
      question: string; // obstruction question for this region, not a navigation command
      maxAgeMs: number; // positive acquisition-age limit at review
      review: "world_master"; // review evidence and coverage; unknown is not a completed inspection
    } }; // Nemeia criteria, not MMO-standard types; each needs an installed validator
interface ObjectiveSpec {
  id: string; // unique within this mission
  description: string; // explains the objective; does not itself prove completion
  dependsOn: readonly string[]; // all named objectives must complete first; no cycles
  optional: boolean; // optional objectives cannot gate required ones
  criterion: ObjectiveCriterion; // measurable outcome, not the agent's execution plan
} // 1–32 objectives, at least one required; validate bound references and dependencies.
// Objectives record milestones. Continuous freshness remains an action check.
// Do not add a generic count until distinct-item identity and deduplication are defined.
03MissionSpec & Missiondescription, objectives and durable lifecycle

The specification records description, objectives and constraints. Runtime validation enforces bounded graphs, known-reference integrity, nonempty descriptions and participant permissions. Objects and places may both be unknown; assignment does not require a complete room map. Assignment is separate from creation.

interface MissionSpec {
  description: string; // World Master's intended outcome and context; not proof of completion
  objectives: readonly ObjectiveSpec[]; // explicit, server-validated completion conditions
  deadlineAt?: Timestamp; // optional world-clock deadline; not a motor timeout
  template?: PackagePin; // optional immutable authoring provenance; inline spec is authoritative
} // No Unit IDs, subscription settings, radius, speed or execution duration.
type MissionState = "active" | "closing" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled";
type MissionOutcome = "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled";
interface Mission {
  id: string; // one accepted instance; a repeat or changed specification uses a new ID
  owner: Identity; // creating World Master, derived from authenticated identity
  spec: MissionSpec; // immutable description, objectives and constraints
  state: { tag: MissionState }; // domain lifecycle, independent of agent focus
  revision: bigint; // lifecycle/assignment fence, not a progress counter
  closingOutcome?: { tag: MissionOutcome }; // pending result while linked physical work closes safely
  createdAt: Timestamp; // initial objective readiness; not the start of robot motion
  updatedAt: Timestamp; // last lifecycle or assignment change
} // A mission remains active while its agent works on another mission.
04MissionFindingevidence-backed search and inspection reports

Agents draft typed findings. This explicit review policy lets a World Master accept identity and inspection judgments while the world validates references, acquisition time and authority. Review also checks that the discovered place matches the mission wording and that the reported extent is supported. The accepted finding lives in objective progress; drafts stay with Eve.

type MissionFinding =
  | { tag: "located"; value: {
      entityId: string; // discovered candidate accepted as the requested object during review
      searchAreaId: string; searchAreaRevision: bigint; // discovered region and exact archived extent/name version
      observationIds: readonly string[]; // nonempty evidence of place identity, object match and location within it
      description: string; // human-readable location; coordinates/time come from cited evidence
    } }
  | { tag: "inspected"; value: {
      regionId: string; regionRevision: bigint; // discovered region and exact archived extent used for the inspection
      conclusion: "obstructed" | "clear" | "unknown"; // a finding, not navigation clearance
      obstructionEntityIds: readonly string[]; // evidenced obstructions; nonempty for obstructed
      observationIds: readonly string[]; // nonempty retained evidence of place identity and reported inspection extent
      description: string; // what was inspected, what was found and any visibility limits
    } };
// Agents draft findings in Eve; drafts are not authoritative world facts or objective progress.
// For these reviewed criteria, only an authenticated World Master can accept a finding.
// The reducer checks criterion/tag, references, authority, freshness and readiness; review supplies judgment.
// An entity PlaceTarget requires the same ID. A description requires reviewed evidence of its referent.
// Unresolved or ambiguous places cannot complete an objective; ask for clarification when evidence cannot decide.
// Located requires an evidenced match and location within the search area; not-found is not success.
// Obstructed requires an evidenced obstruction in the region. Clear requires whole-region coverage and no obstruction IDs.
// Unknown or insufficient coverage cannot complete inspection. Review never invents sensor evidence.
// Store the accepted finding in mission_objective_progress.evidence and reviewer identity in audit.
05ObjectiveProgress & MissionEvidencepending or completed, with retained proof

Progress validation reads domain records inside the transaction. Unknown, pruned, out-of-scope or too-old evidence cannot complete an objective. After acceptance, the milestone remains completed; live action checks still use fresh evidence.

type MissionEvidence =
  | { tag: "observation"; value: { observationId: string } } // load retained acquisition, association and requested facet
  | { tag: "execution"; value: { executionId: string } } // load matching measured outcome and safe-closure receipt
  | { tag: "finding"; value: MissionFinding }; // reviewed criteria only; World Master acceptance and retained references required
type ObjectiveProgress =
  | { objectiveId: string; status: "pending" } // no accepted proof; readiness is derived separately
  | { objectiveId: string; status: "completed";
      evidence: MissionEvidence; // validated proof, not an LLM success assertion
      recordedAt: Timestamp; // authoritative progress commit time
    }; // read projection; pending entries need no persisted row
// mission_objective_progress stores one immutable completion proof per mission/objective.
// Repeated submission returns the first accepted proof; it never increments a counter.
// One observation may support multiple objectives only when each validator independently accepts it.
// Completion remains recorded as evidence ages; future actions still require fresh measurements.
06Example · approach and resampleparallel evidence and dependent outcomes

Resolve the entity before activation. Geometry and semantic evidence arrive independently; both unlock approach. A fresh observation after arrival satisfies the final objective. Navigation must meet the action's local spatial requirements.

export const inspectionSpec: MissionSpec = {
  description: "Approach the known backpack, then acquire fresh geometry",
  // hardware policy belongs to installed action bindings, not the mission
  objectives: [
    { id: "geometry", description: "Acquire target geometry", dependsOn: [], optional: false,
      criterion: { tag: "observed", value: { entityId: "backpack-A", facet: { tag: "geometry" }, maxAgeMs: 500 } } },
    { id: "semantics", description: "Acquire target hypotheses", dependsOn: [], optional: false,
      criterion: { tag: "observed", value: { entityId: "backpack-A", facet: { tag: "semantic" }, maxAgeMs: 2_000 } } },
    { id: "approach", description: "Reach the measured standoff", dependsOn: ["geometry", "semantics"], optional: false,
      criterion: { tag: "approached", value: { targetId: "backpack-A", standoffM: 0.8 } } },
    { id: "resample", description: "Acquire geometry after arrival", dependsOn: ["approach"], optional: false,
      criterion: { tag: "observed", value: { entityId: "backpack-A", facet: { tag: "geometry" }, maxAgeMs: 500 } } },
  ],
}; // geometry and semantics can progress in parallel; resample needs new evidence after approach credit
// These are outcome dependencies, not navigation commands or a model's internal plan.
07MissionLogone agent, multiple assigned missions

The mission board is a read projection, like a quest log. It does not duplicate mission state, assign Units or create an Eve session per mission.

interface MissionLog {
  agentId: string; // one logical agent can have several assigned missions at once
  entries: readonly MissionView[]; // authorized assignments and retained outcomes, ordered by stable mission ID
} // Derived quest-log-style view, also called the mission board; not an audit log or new table.
// World Master assigns missions. The agent chooses its next work across this log.
// A compact summary covers every assignment; authorized reads supply deeper details.
// Choosing a focus neither pauses other missions nor changes their objectives or deadlines.
// Independent outcomes can progress while the agent is reasoning about another mission.
// The shared Unit reservation prevents conflicting physical work across the entire log.
02c / Agents, Units & coordination

Agents, Units & coordination

World Masters assign missions and Unit authority. Agents coordinate work through mission logs and shared facts; systems handle perception, mapping and execution at independent cadences.

01Visibility, assignment & reservationthree different permissions and state boundaries

Visibility determines which recorded facts a client may read. Assignment determines which agent may request named actions on a Unit. Reservation records which accepted execution currently occupies that Unit. Seeing a Unit does not permit control; owning its assignment does not mean it is available. One agent owns command rights per Unit, with any number of authorized observers/advisers. Measured state is written by authorized systems, never by its assigned agent.

read scope ≠ Unit control grant ≠ execution reservation
02Cooperation & messagesshared facts first; chat for requests and explanations

Agents coordinate through shared objectives, Unit assignments, active executions and measured outcomes. An addressed message can request help, propose a handoff or explain a decision. It cannot transfer control, reserve a Unit or declare an objective complete. Use the validated world operation for those effects. An optional coordinator agent is a strategy choice, not a required new role. The World Master remains responsible for changes to mission participation and authority.

message proposes → authorized operation commits → subscriptions notify
03Reassignment, pause & expiryrevoke authority without inventing physical closure

A World Master can pause an agent or change its assignments. Bump the affected revision, invalidate pending proposals, block new admission/claim and request cancellation of affected attempts. Expiry follows the same rule, including when no new observations arrive. Retain the physical reservation until the local executor confirms safe closure; a new agent must wait. Assignment revision fences decision authority; controller epoch fences the physical executor. Neither alone can stop disconnected hardware, so local watchdogs remain required.

revoke old rights → cancel/reconcile old work → safe release → new claim
04Three independent clocksRTS-level intent above continuous systems

World Masters govern missions. Agents choose strategy and coordinate resources when useful. Perception systems continuously refresh evidence; pathfinding and control systems execute bounded actions at their own rates. A slow LLM does not slow localization or motor control. Fast classification need not create a new agent. Use task-specific measured cadences, meaningful-change triggers and timers rather than a single global tick or assumed fixed frequency.

observation updates · deliberate decisions · robot-local control
03 / Service contracts

Service contracts

Typed boundaries for world storage, perception, missions, coordination and execution. Each contract defines authority, validation and retry behavior; it need not be a separate microservice.

01WorldMemorydurable local map and recovery

The world stores frame-qualified knowledge and retained checkpoint heads. A trusted mapper/storage boundary verifies evidence and immutable bytes before a compare-and-set commit. SLAM and blob storage stay outside database transactions; local mapping does not require a global frame.

interface WorldMemory {
  createLocalMap(input: { id: string; unitId: string; rootFrameId: string }): Promise<void>; // authorized mapper; register a unique frame epoch and durable map identity
  commitMapRevision(input: {
    mapId: string; expectedRevision: bigint; // compare-and-set prevents concurrent checkpoint heads
    manifest: ResourceRef; // immutable retained manifest and complete verified reference closure
  }): Promise<bigint>; // identical manifest retry returns its revision; otherwise atomically advance head + audit
  readLocalMap(input: { mapId: string; revision?: bigint }): Promise<LocalMapView>; // authorized checkpoint plus current frame-qualified records
  projectRegion(input: {
    entityId: string; mapId: string; expectedRevision: bigint; // trusted spatial worker; zero creates a region component
    extent: RegionExtent; observationIds: readonly string[]; // validate retained checkpoint, aligned mask and spatial evidence
  }): Promise<void>; // compare revision; commit extent + evidence + audit, preserving any assigned name
  nameRegion(input: {
    entityId: string; expectedRevision: bigint; name: string | null; // World Master only; null clears the assigned name
  }): Promise<void>; // bound nonempty text; derive author/time; bump region revision + audit without changing geometry
} // No SLAM, blob IO or inference runs in the transaction.
// Region edits archive the prior component and preserve proof references; name changes never rewrite evidence.
// A trusted storage/mapper boundary verifies retained bytes before the commit. Reducers verify its receipt.
// Observation ingestion has its own idempotent commits; map checkpoints record their exact input coverage.
// Restore persisted state after restart; require new localization evidence before spatial action.
02Missionsaccepted specification → verified progress → safe closure

World Masters create and cancel missions. Assigned active agents can contribute validated proof to the shared ledger. Validate bounded graphs, known references, nonempty place descriptions and future deadlines. Unresolved place names do not prevent creation or assignment. Located and inspected findings require the specified World Master review; hardware choice and motion limits stay outside MissionSpec. Reconciliation is idempotent and scheduled even without sensor writes.

interface Missions {
  createMission(input: { id: string; spec: MissionSpec }): Promise<void>; // World Master only; validate objectives, known references, nonempty place descriptions and deadline; activate + audit
  readMissionLog(input: { agentId: string }): Promise<MissionLog>; // own agent or authorized World Master; projected from assignments, missions and progress
  recordObjectiveProgress(input: { missionId: string; objectiveId: string; evidence: MissionEvidence }): Promise<void>; // validate proof/readiness and criterion-specific authority; atomically record progress + audit and request closure if required objectives complete
  cancelMission(input: { missionId: string; expectedRevision: bigint }): Promise<void>; // record cancellation, block new work and reconcile linked executions
  reconcileMission(input: { missionId: string }): Promise<void>; // enforce deadline/completion; terminal result requires confirmed safe physical closure
} // Descriptive service boundary, not a separate microservice or handwritten transport.
// Read views/subscriptions maintain the mission log; assignment is a WorldMasters operation.
// Agents submit observation/execution references. Reviewed findings require a World Master's authenticated acceptance.
// No caller can submit status flags, percentages or mutable success counters.
03WorldMastersmission teams, read scope and Unit assignments

Only an enrolled World Master may administer agents and mission participation or grant Unit control. Bootstrap platform credentials remain the administrator's job. Revisions fence stale proposals. Revocation, pause and grant expiry block new admission/claim and request cancellation of affected attempts. A transfer retains the execution reservation until confirmed local closure; timers enforce expiry even without incoming observations. No new Unit owner can steal running hardware.

export interface WorldMasters {
  configureAgent(input: Omit<Row<"agent">, "revision">, expectedRevision: bigint): Promise<void>; // enroll an agent principal or edit read scope/pause; server assigns revision; zero expects creation
  assignMission(input: { missionId: string; agentId: string; active: boolean; expectedRevision: bigint }): Promise<void>; // validate roster edit; bump mission revision; reconcile revoked agent's linked attempts
  assignUnit(input: { unitId: string; agentId?: string; actionNames: string[]; expiresAt?: Timestamp; expectedRevision: bigint }): Promise<void>; // compare grant revision; revoke old authority, bump revision and cancel/reconcile affected work
} // World Master is an authorized client role, not a mandatory service or singleton; paused agents cannot start new work
// Ownership transfer and grant expiry are NOT physical stop; reservation stays until the local executor confirms safety.
// World Masters inspect the whole recorded world but cannot rewrite measured evidence or bypass local interlocks.
04AgentCoordinationaddressed team messages

Messages carry durable bounded text between authorized participants, never evidence or control grants. Subscription interests are derived by Nemeia from Unit assignments; agents have no subscription-management operation.

interface AgentCoordination {
  sendMessage(input: { id: string; missionId: string; toAgentId: string; content: string }): Promise<void>; // authenticate sender, validate participants and retain bounded messages
} // No subscription-management API: Nemeia derives awareness from Unit assignments and world-managed policy.
// Messages support coordination; they cannot grant control or declare objectives complete.
05PerceptionIngressobservations → association and current components

Authorize producer identity, package/session and owned facets. Compare identical retry bodies before assigning identities. Validate clock error, transforms, endpoints, supersedes references and monotonic facet times. Commit observation, track binding, supplied component changes and audit together.

export interface PerceptionIngress {
  ingestObservation(input: ObservationInput): Promise<void>; // authorize producer; associate; atomically update supplied facets + audit
} // identical ID + principal + input retries are no-ops; changed duplicates conflict
06ActionRequestsa valid request becomes one accepted execution

Same caller, execution ID and body is a retry; a changed body conflicts. Check current agent, mission readiness/revision and the Unit grant for the requested action. approach@1 pins target geometry; navigate@1 names a map-derived pose and its basis checkpoint. Revalidate the pose against current mapping/localization and independent exploration limits. Neither a room name nor a retained map grants motion permission. Check deadlines, installed policy, stop state and fresh required evidence. Reject concurrent attempts for the same mission/objective. Arrival cannot complete located or inspected. World Master interventions retain the same physical gates.

export interface ActionRequests {
  requestNavigate(input: NavigateRequest): Promise<void>; // validate local pose, map context and exploration authority; accept navigate@1
  requestApproach(input: ApproachRequest): Promise<void>; // validate policy and evidence; insert one accepted execution + audit
} // duplicate same caller/body returns the existing receipt even after acceptBy; it does not run again
07ExecutionClaimsreserve one Unit before physical IO

Only the bound controller can claim. In one transaction recheck mission readiness/revision, current requester role, participation, agent pause, Unit assignment/revision/expiry, deadline, evidence and target pin; reserve the Unit and set running. Assignment revision and local controller epoch are different fences. Use acceptBy as the claim deadline too. An existing claim remains reconcilable after expiry; that never permits restarting cancelled work.

export interface ExecutionClaims {
  claimExecution(input: {
    executionId: string; // accepted attempt, or an identical claim retry by this controller
    controllerEpoch: bigint; // must match unit_control AND the local controller's persisted generation
  }): Promise<void>; // recheck pins/freshness; reserve unit and set running in the same transaction
} // do not steal a running attempt on timeout; a database fence alone cannot stop a physical robot
08Cancellationrequest safe closure, not instant physical stop

The requesting agent may cancel its own attempt, including after assignment revocation; a World Master may intervene. Set cancelling and audit atomically. The controller confirms safe closure before terminal cancellation. Even an unclaimed attempt needs confirmation it never started; expiry alone is not proof.

export interface Cancellation {
  cancelExecution(input: { executionId: string }): Promise<void>; // transition accepted/running to cancelling; never imply physical stop
} // local controller confirms safe state before cancellation becomes terminal
09ControlFeedbackproject measured controller state

Only the enrolled controller and current epoch can report. Reject stale/future reports. A remote false stopLatched value never clears the actual local latch. Keep unit reservations if safe state is unknown.

export interface ControlFeedback {
  reportControl(input: {
    unitId: string; controllerEpoch: bigint; // authenticated local executor, not the assigned reasoning agent
    observedAt: Timestamp; // control acquisition time, not report arrival time
    stopLatched: boolean; safeStateConfirmed: boolean; // measured local state; uncertainty stays explicit
  }): Promise<void>; // update unit_control; cannot claim, clear a local latch or authorize motion
}
10ExecutionCompletionmeasured outcome → immutable terminal receipt

Verify controller ownership, epoch and matching action/result types. Approach checks measured Unit/target distance and target-motion policy; navigation checks the final Unit pose against installed position and heading tolerances. Both require fresh applicable measurements and a durable local safe-closure receipt. Cancellation wins once cancelling is committed. Unknown physical state retains the reservation until reconciliation.

export interface ExecutionCompletion {
  finishExecution(input: {
    executionId: string; controllerEpoch: bigint; // same claimed attempt and controller generation
    result: ActionCompletion; // success includes measurement IDs and a durable safe-closure receipt
  }): Promise<void>; // validate outcome, commit terminal state + audit, release the active unit only if safe
} // if cancelling committed first, reject success; reconcile cancellation or failure instead
11WorldAdministrationexplicit provisioning and lifecycle

Restrict enrollment and binding installation to administrators. Reducers enforce relationship integrity; there is no assumed SQL foreign-key cascade. Refuse entity removal while active executions depend on it. New control generations require a verified local stop and persisted local fence, not just an incremented database counter.

export interface WorldAdministration {
  putMember(input: Row<"member">): Promise<void>; // admin-only enrollment; bound role, Unit and producer package
  installAction(input: Row<"actionBinding">): Promise<void>; // admin-only installation; increment version; never mutate an active pin
  removeEntity(input: { entityId: string }): Promise<void>; // reject active references; tombstone and remove components/relations atomically
  reconcileController(input: { unitId: string; newController: Identity; newEpoch: bigint; receiptId: string }): Promise<void>; // only after local safe stop and fence installation are verified
} // provisioning establishes the first admin out of band; never expose an unauthenticated bootstrap reducer
12LocalControllerrobot-local durability, limits and stop

This boundary stays outside SpacetimeDB. Use an existing navigation stack/driver, OS supervision, local persistent receipts and a monotonic watchdog. After a crash, reconcile receipts before delivery. Do not time out and reassign a physical attempt while an old worker may still be acting.

export interface LocalController {
  reconcile(executionId: string): Promise<LocalReceipt | undefined>; // inspect persistent outcome before considering any delivery
  start(input: {
    executionId: string; controllerEpoch: bigint; // immutable idempotency key plus installed local fence
    request: ActionIntent; binding: Row<"actionBinding">; // exact accepted intent and tighter local limits
  }): Promise<LocalReceipt>; // persist before IO, reject changed duplicates, then bounded local navigation
  cancel(executionId: string): Promise<LocalReceipt>; // enter safe state locally; works without the world database
  stop(reason: string): Promise<LocalReceipt>; // latch stop locally first; do not depend on a subscription or cloud call
}
export interface LocalReceipt {
  id: string; executionId: string; controllerEpoch: bigint; // stable receipt identity and attempt correlation
  outcome: "notStarted" | "running" | "succeeded" | "cancelled" | "failed" | "unknown"; // sent is never succeeded
  safeState: "confirmed" | "unknown"; // uncertainty blocks new physical attempts
} // robot-local durable storage, not an extra remote table; independent monotonic watchdog and OS supervision
13EvidenceStorageretained bytes stay off the state path

Media continues over the appropriate streaming transport. Retained images, masks, clouds and meshes use existing blob storage. Only validated immutable references enter the world; credentials and expiring download URLs do not become component values.

export interface EvidenceStorage {
  resolve(resourceId: string): Promise<{ url: string; expiresAt: Timestamp }>; // authenticated access to retained bytes; explicit missing/expired result
} // existing blob storage and media transport; no image/cloud byte arrays in live component tables
04 / Database tables

Database tables

23 private tables hold world records, local maps, assignments, progress and execution receipts. Authorized views expose the relevant state to each client. Eve owns conversation and runtime persistence.

01world_configworld identity, clock and awareness policy
NameTypeDescription
idu8PK. Singleton key = 0; one database owns one world.
worldIdstringunique. Stable world identity; database names may change.
modeModeNever mix live timestamps and simulation time in one database.
clockErrorBoundMsu32Maximum accepted acquisition-clock uncertainty.
awarenessPolicyAwarenessPolicyWorld-managed batching and optional metric radius; not agent-owned entity filters.

One singleton row. No mandatory global frame. World-managed awareness includes direct Unit observations; an optional radius adds spatial interest when localization permits. Changing a radius neither grants access nor changes entity identity.

02membercaller roles, scope and producer provenance
NameTypeDescription
identityIdentityPK. Verified SpacetimeDB caller; never trust a submitted principal ID.
roleRoleOne role per identity; use separate worker credentials.
unitIdOption<string>Controller/perception scope; absent for decision clients and world-wide roles.
producerSessionOption<string>Current worker session; restart creates a new identity for tracks.
packageOption<PackagePin>Authorized producer code; asserted during deployment, not caller-selected.

All base tables are private. Membership gates public views and reducer permissions. Bootstrap administration through deployment, never an open signup reducer.

03entitystable identity and lifecycle
NameTypeDescription
idstringPK. Opaque UUID; never inferred from the detected label.
displayNamestringHuman-readable name; no authority or association meaning.
kindstringDescriptive deployment vocabulary, e.g. robot, object or region; never confers controllability.
createdAtTimestampDatabase creation time, not sensor time.
removedAtOption<Timestamp>Tombstone prevents identity reuse; readers exclude removed entities.

All component/relation writes validate live entity references. Tombstone removal atomically deletes current components and incident relations; never recycle IDs.

04posecurrent frame-qualified position estimates
NameTypeDescription
keystringPK. Canonical tuple [entityId, frameId]; one owning projection pipeline per facet/frame.
entityIdstringIndexed entity identity; retain independent local-frame estimates instead of one global value.
frameIdstringRegistered local reference frame and reset epoch; no shared world frame required.
valuePose3Measured translation and unit quaternion.
observedAtTimestampAcquisition time; polling never refreshes it.
observationIdstringExact evidence in observation or its retained archive.
versionu64Monotonic revision within this entity/frame facet; action pins identify the frame and revision.

Key by entity and registered frame, not one global pose per entity. One authorized projection owner per facet/frame. Compare times only within the correct stream/frame epoch; a delayed poll is not fresh evidence.

05geometrylocal spatial or image geometry
NameTypeDescription
keystringPK. Canonical tuple [entityId, frameId]; one owning projection pipeline per facet/frame.
entityIdstringIndexed entity identity; retain independent local-frame estimates instead of one global value.
frameIdstringRegistered local/sensor frame; 2D geometry still refers to its exact image and remains in pixels.
valueGeometryGeometry with its native frame; image boxes do not imply metric position or navigability.
observedAtTimestampGeometry acquisition time independent of semantic evidence.
observationIdstringObservation that supplied this geometry.
versionu64Monotonic revision within this entity/frame facet; action pins identify the frame and revision.

Preserve estimates in their own registered frame. A 2D box remains image-space evidence. An approach@1 action requires a usable local 3D target and transform to the executor; it does not require a universally shared world frame.

06semanticclassification hypotheses
NameTypeDescription
entityIdstringPK. Classification attaches to identity, not vice versa.
valueSemanticLabels and scores; no invented collision shape or action capability.
observedAtTimestampSemantic acquisition time, not the latest geometry time.
observationIdstringEvidence that supplied the hypotheses.
versionu64Independent semantic component revision.

Independent update frequency and timestamps. Scores must be finite and in [0,1]. Do not interpret semantic confidence as geometry certainty.

07relationdirected domain facts
NameTypeDescription
keystringPK. Canonical JSON tuple [subjectId,predicate,objectId]; collision-safe encoding.
subjectIdstringindexed. Existing, non-removed source entity.
predicatestringInstalled domain meaning, e.g. observed_by; not free-form authorization.
objectIdstringindexed. Existing, non-removed destination entity.
observationIdOption<string>Evidence for an observed relation; absent for configured relations.

Reducers check both endpoints and installed predicate meanings. JSON tuple encoding avoids delimiter collisions. Evidence references are optional only for configured facts.

08observationbounded evidence and retry history
NameTypeDescription
idstringPK. Same UUID as input.id; deduplicate before assigning an entity.
producerIdentityctx.sender, bound to an authorized producer role and package.
packagePackagePinImmutable code provenance copied from member at ingestion.
unitIdstringOriginating Unit derived from authenticated producer scope; preserve across credential/session changes.
localMapIdstringOriginating map context checked at ingestion; unlocated evidence remains attached without fabricated coordinates.
entityIdstringindexed. Recorded association decision, never recomputed on replay.
inputObservationInputSupplied facets, original times, frames, transforms and fusion references.
recordedAtTimestampDatabase receipt time; not evidence freshness.

Record association and provenance once. Identical producer/body retries are no-ops. Archive before pruning references needed by current components or decisions; reject replay outside the retained retry horizon.

09trackproducer-scoped association
NameTypeDescription
keystringPK. Canonical JSON tuple [producerIdentity,producerSession,trackId].
entityIdstringindexed. Associated entity; session changes do not merge same-label objects.
lastObservationIdstringLatest accepted evidence for this association.

Tracking restarts use new sessions. No same-label merges. Prune dead sessions only when doing so cannot permit an old observation to create a duplicate entity.

10action_bindinginstalled typed action policy per Unit
NameTypeDescription
keystringPK. Canonical tuple [unitId, actionName]; each installed action has its own policy.
unitIdstringIndexed controllable entity; bindings share its single execution reservation.
actionNameapproach@1 | navigate@1Typed action implemented by this pinned executor; never supplied as arbitrary code.
versionu64Immutable revision copied into accepted executions.
executorPackagePinExact installed implementation; never chosen by the requesting client.
modeModeSimulation or physical implementation of the same action meaning.
maxEvidenceAgeMsu32Maximum age of required Unit/localization evidence and target geometry when applicable.
maxLinearMpsf64Positive configured speed cap; local gate can impose a tighter cap.
maxRunMsu32Bounded execution duration measured locally with a monotonic clock.
toleranceMf64Positive finite position error for navigation, or error around an approach standoff.
headingToleranceRadOption<f64>Required positive finite heading tolerance for navigate@1; absent for approach@1.

Key by Unit and action name. Each execution retains its accepted binding. Approach and pose navigation share one Unit reservation; the controller installs footprint, traversal checks and tighter local limits.

11unit_controlone controller and active attempt per robot
NameTypeDescription
unitIdstringPK. Same entity ID as the Unit; local executor ownership, not agent assignment.
controllerIdentityAllowed claimant and feedback producer for this robot.
epochu64Fencing generation also enforced by the persistent local controller.
activeExecutionIdOption<string>At most one active physical attempt; claim updates this atomically.
stopLatchedboolProjection of the local stop latch; false is not proof of permission to move.
safeStateConfirmedboolLast measured controller confirmation; retain uncertainty on lost feedback.
observedAtTimestampAcquisition time of the local control report.

This is a database projection, not the emergency-stop authority. The local controller independently enforces the same fencing generation and can always stop without the database.

12missionaccepted specification and durable lifecycle
NameTypeDescription
idstringPK. One accepted mission instance; same owner/id/spec retry returns this row.
ownerIdentityindexed. Creating World Master principal; provenance, not a single-agent ownership lock.
specMissionSpecMissionSpec: immutable description, objectives and optional deadline/template; no hardware assignment.
stateMissionStateactive -> closing -> succeeded/failed/cancelled; terminals are immutable.
revisionu64Starts at 1; bumps on lifecycle or roster changes, not every evidence credit.
closingOutcomeOption<MissionOutcome>Present only while closing; cancellation can replace pending success.
createdAtTimestampActivation time; no implicit credit for evidence predating readiness.
updatedAtTimestampLast lifecycle or roster change, not a heartbeat or sensor timestamp.

World Master authorship, shared team progress. Repeat/changed intent uses a new ID; strategy and assignment may change independently. Lifecycle or roster edits bump revision. Removal rejects targets referenced by active/closing missions. Unknown physical outcomes keep the mission closing.

13mission_objective_progressvalidated completion evidence for each objective
NameTypeDescription
keystringPK. Canonical tuple [missionId, objectiveId]; one immutable completion proof, not a counter.
missionIdstringindexed. Existing mission; validated World Master/participant and evidence access.
objectiveIdstringExisting objective in mission.spec; dependencies were ready when evidence occurred.
evidenceMissionEvidenceMissionEvidence loaded and validated by the world; a submitted status or percentage cannot advance progress.
recordedAtTimestampCompletion commit time; pending objectives are derived from the specification and need no row.

One immutable row per completed mission/objective. Pending entries derive from MissionSpec; there is no writable status, percentage or duplicate counter. Validate retained proof and dependency readiness; preserve the first accepted proof on retries. The mission log joins this table with missions and assignments, without its own storage table.

14agentlogical decision-maker and administrative configuration
NameTypeDescription
idstringPK. Durable logical decision-maker; neither entity ID nor connection ID.
principalIdentityunique. One enrolled agent credential; authenticate requests against this mapping.
displayNamestringHuman-readable name, never authority.
readScopeReadScopeWorld Master grant; interest filters may narrow but never widen it.
pausedboolAdministrative hold; separate from idle/ready/thinking/waiting and transport health.
revisionu64Bump on administrative changes; invalidate active contexts and recheck proposals.

One agent can serve multiple missions and control multiple Units. Credentials belong to enrolled agent principals, not robots. Read scope, subscription interest and execution authority are separate. Scope/pause edits bump revision and invalidate affected contexts. No online flag is used as command authority.

15mission_agentmany-to-many mission participation
NameTypeDescription
